title: The /trade calculator never sums the canonical board: the frontend posts an explicit tep_multiplier=1.15 on every load, which disables the ADR-015 TE basis conversion and reprices 129 of 809 players by up to -21.2%
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md ADR-015: TE rows from non-TEP sources are lifted via te_premium.convert_te_value using KTC's measured uplift (1.209 at the top rising toward 2.05), replacing 'a flat 1.15 that sat below the entire observed range'; the feature ships flag-ON. CLAUDE.md also states 'an explicit operator slider value bypasses the curve regardless' — but does not note that the frontend always sends one. useSettings.js additionally claims tepMultiplier=null means 'auto from league / inherit from backend'.
observed: data_contract.py gates the whole basis conversion behind `if not tep_multiplier_is_override:`. `useSettings.js` SETTINGS_DEFAULTS sets tepMultiplier: 1.15 (a finite number), and readSettings() actively coerces null/1.0/1.25 back to 1.15 on first read. tepMultiplierIsCustomized() returns true for any finite number, so fetchDynastyData takes the override path and POSTs {"tep_multiplier":1.15} on EVERY page load. Captured live from the browser on /trade: `POST /api/rankings/overrides?view=delta {"tep_multiplier":1.15}`. The response reports tepMultiplier 1.15, tepMultiplierDefault 1.15, tepMultiplierDerived 1.15, isCustomized false — identical declared parameters to the base contract — but tepMultiplierSource flips 'default' -> 'override' and 129 of 809 players get different values. The ADR-015 curve is therefore unreachable from the product: no user-facing path produces the board the backend calls canonical.

reproduction.expected: Posting the exact value the server reports as tepMultiplierDerived/tepMultiplierDefault must be a no-op: 0 of 809 players differ (which is what an empty body {} does).
reproduction.actual: 129 of 809 differ. Tyler Conklin 1450 -> 1142 (-21.2%), Josh Cuevas 1541 -> 1215 (-21.2%), Sam LaPorta 5222 -> 5021 (-3.8%). 89 players >5%, 54 >10%. Confirmed in the DOM: /trade renders Sam LaPorta at 5,021, /api/dynasty-data says 5,222.

userImpact: Every TE priced on the trade calculator, the rankings board and every client-side sum is up to 21% below the value the backend's own canonical pipeline produces, with no indication on screen. A user trading a TE gives one away ~20% too cheap (or overpays to acquire one) on a board the app cannot be configured to leave — clearing the setting is undone by the readSettings() migration. The measured TE-basis feature the repo shipped and flagged ON is dead in production.

priorFinding.note: No area-2 prior finding covers the TEP override path or the base-vs-override board divergence. Adjacent but distinct from PRIOR-A02-F11 (which is about KTC constants being fed our blended values, not about which blend).

whatWorks: POST /api/rankings/overrides?view=delta with an empty body {} reproduces the base contract exactly (0 of 812 rows differ) — the delta merge itself is sound. The response honestly stamps tepMultiplierSource so the divergence is diagnosable from the payload.
rootCause: src/api/data_contract.py:6939 gates te_basis_conversion on `not tep_multiplier_is_override`, and the frontend's default settings make every request an override. The gate was written for 'the operator moved the slider'; nothing checks whether the posted value equals the derived default, and the frontend has no 'unset' state because readSettings() rewrites null back to 1.15.
requiredRepair: Either (a) make tepMultiplier default to null and stop the readSettings() coercion so fetchDynastyData takes the no-override path, or (b) treat a posted value equal to tepMultiplierDerived as 'default' rather than 'override' in data_contract.py's source resolution. (a) is smaller and matches the documented sentinel. Add a regression test asserting POST {tep_multiplier: <derived>} is byte-identical to POST {}.
dependencies: Interacts with W08-F012 (backend engines read the un-overridden board) — fixing this closes that divergence too.

title: The Value Adjustment tooltip tells the user the bonus goes to 'the side with fewer pieces', but 46.7% of fired VAs go to a side with equal or MORE pieces
claimUnderTest: SideCard renders title="Consolidation / roster-spot premium: the side with fewer pieces frees a roster spot, so KTC-style math adds this bonus on top of the raw total." The same file's own algorithm docstring contradicts it: 'KTC's algorithm is symmetric: equal-count trades (e.g. 2v2 stud-vs-pile) fire VA when one side has bigger studs.'
observed: ktcAdjustPackage awards the VA on raw_adj INTENSITY (e/team1Total vs a/team2Total — i.e. which side's value is concentrated in bigger studs), not on piece count. Piece count only enters through the progressive nerf and the 1v1 suppression. Over 50,000 random 1-4 vs 1-4 trades built from the live board, the VA fired 21,610 times: 11,524 (53.3%) to the side with fewer pieces, 6,815 (31.5%) on equal counts, 3,271 (15.1%) to the side with MORE pieces. Concrete live case: A=[Bijan Robinson 9706, Tyjae Spears 2121, Jessie Bates 1707, Kyle Hamilton 3062] (4 pieces) vs B=[Jadarian Price 4286, Dak Prescott 5519, 2028 Late 1st 4079] (3 pieces) -> VA 3,815 credited to A, the side with MORE pieces. Equal-count case: 4v4 with Puka Nacua on side A -> VA 5,093 to A, 29% of its raw total.

reproduction.command: cd docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W08 && node vacopy.mjs   # source in evidence/W08/va-recipient.json; regenerate by importing ktcAdjustPackage from frontend/lib/trade-logic.js and sampling the live board
reproduction.expected: If the tooltip is true, 100% of fired VAs land on the side with strictly fewer pieces.
reproduction.actual: 53.3% fewer, 31.5% equal, 15.1% more (n=21,610 fired VAs over 50,000 sampled trades).

inputs.side_sizes: 1-4 per side, assets drawn from the 812 priced live board rows

userImpact: The user reads the only explanation the page offers for a bonus worth up to 5,093 points (29% of a side's raw total) and is told a rule that is false half the time. They cannot predict the verdict, and when the VA lands on the bigger pile the explanation directly contradicts what they can see on screen.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A02-F13 asserts 'docstrings and status docs describe behaviour the code does not implement' generically; this is a specific user-facing tooltip with a measured falsification rate.

whatWorks: The VA number itself is correct: ktcAdjustPackage is a faithful port (see W08-F010) and the SideCard honestly decomposes the headline as 'Raw N + VA M' rather than hiding it.
rootCause: The tooltip was written against the retired V2/V13 consolidation-premium model (a piece-count formula) and was not updated when the 2026-04-26 direct KTC port replaced it with an intensity-based rule.
requiredRepair: Rewrite the tooltip to describe what the code does: 'KTC-style adjustment: the side whose value is concentrated in fewer, bigger pieces gets a bonus, because a stud is worth more than the same total spread across depth.' Do not mention roster spots — no roster-spot term exists in ktcProcessV.

title: Adding a positive-value asset to your side can lower your side's total and flip the verdict against you — the fairness gap is non-monotonic in 1.1-1.9% of trades
claimUnderTest: adjustedSideTotals returns `adjusted = raw + adjustment`, and TradeMeter/verdictFromGap render the verdict off `adjustedA - adjustedB`. The implicit contract of a trade calculator is that adding value to a side improves that side's position.
observed: Because the VA is a discontinuous function of the piece SET (1v1 suppression, the 3.3% display floor, the progressive nerf, and the branch switch on raw_adj intensity), adding one positive-value asset to side A can reduce A's adjusted total. Over 40,000 random 1-3 vs 1-3 trades from the live board, 772 (1.93%) got WORSE for A after adding a real asset to A; 27 of those crossed a meter-verdict label boundary. Restricting to multi-asset shapes only (2-3 per side, so the 1v1 suppression rule cannot explain it), 687 of 60,000 (1.15%) still violate. Live example (all values are live board values): A=[2026 Pick 1.04 5320, Jadarian Price 4286, Dont'e Thornton 1509] vs B=[T.J. Hockenson 3107, 2026 Pick 2.09 2846, Kaden Elliss 1869]; gap +4903 with a 1,610 VA on A. Add Boye Mafe (1,235 board points) to A -> A's VA drops to 0 and the gap FALLS to +4528. Verdict-flipping example: A=[Daiyan Henley 1923] vs B=[2028 Late 2nd 2785], gap -862 = SLIGHT EDGE; add Omar Speights (894) to A -> gap -1219 = UNFAIR.

reproduction.command: cd docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W08 && node mono2.mjs && node mono3.mjs
reproduction.expected: For every trade T and every asset x with value(x) > 0: gap(A+x, B) >= gap(A, B). Violations: 0.
reproduction.actual: 772 / 40,000 (1.93%) for 1-3 per side; 687 / 60,000 (1.15%) for 2-3 per side; 27 verdict-label flips.

userImpact: The user follows the page's own signal — 'you are behind, add something' — adds a real asset, and the verdict moves further against them with no explanation. On the 27 measured flips the badge goes from SLIGHT EDGE to UNFAIR (or UNFAIR to LOPSIDED) as a direct result of the user giving MORE. They will then remove a good asset or demand more back, which is the wrong negotiating move.

priorFinding.note: F10 framed this as a balancer-selection bug ('sized against a VA-inclusive gap but selected by raw value') and illustrated it with a hand-built 1-for-many shape. Confirmed and generalised: the non-monotonicity is a property of adjustedSideTotals itself, independent of findBalancers, and I measured its rate on the live board (1.15% for multi-asset shapes where the 1v1 suppression cannot be the cause) plus 27 verdict-label flips. F10's proposed cause (balancers select on raw value) is necessary but not sufficient — no selection rule fixes a non-monotonic objective.

whatWorks: The gap is exactly A/B symmetric (see W08-F009), so the non-monotonicity is not an ordering artifact.
rootCause: The VA is folded into the side totals (`adjusted = raw + adjustment`) and then differenced, but ktcAdjustPackage is a step function of the piece multiset with three discontinuities (1v1 suppression, the |value|/(totalA+totalB) < 0.033 display floor, and the branch switch on h vs y). KTC itself displays the VA as an advisory 'add this much to even it out' badge, not as an addend to a side total — folding it into the meter is what turns the discontinuity into a verdict flip.
requiredRepair: Either stop folding the VA into `adjusted` and render it as KTC does (an advisory line beside a raw-total verdict), or clamp: compute the VA, and if adding an asset to a side would reduce that side's adjusted total, hold the previous VA and surface a note. The first is smaller and matches the source the port is faithful to.
dependencies: Compounds with PRIOR-A02-F02 (absolute fairness bands), which is what makes the 27 label flips reachable at small gaps.

title: Current-year (2026) draft picks cannot be found in the trade calculator's only search box — the exclusion is a hardcoded /^2026\b/ regex, not the contract's currentDraftYear
claimUnderTest: The trade page presents one 'Search to add to Side A…' input per side as the primary way to build a trade; the board carries 72 slot-specific 2026 pick rows (2026 Pick 1.01 … 6.12) with live values (1.01 = 7,799).
observed: searchAssets() filters out every row matching `r.assetClass === 'pick' && /^2026\b/.test(r.name)`. Measured in a real browser through request interception: typing '2026' or '2026 Pick 1.0' into the Side A search box returns ZERO results, while '2027 Mid 1st' returns '2027 Mid 1st PICK #48.0 · 5,606' and '2029 Early 1st' returns '#79.0 · 2,668'. The same hardcoded regex also removes 2026 picks from both balancer pools (page.jsx:740/753 and 785/794). The contract exposes currentDraftYear (2026) and page.jsx:295 already resolves it into a `currentDraftYear` memo — the four exclusion sites do not use it, so the filter will exclude the wrong year from 2027 onward.

reproduction.command: cd docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W08 && /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket/.venv/bin/python page_probe2.py   # then read queries['2026'] and queries['2027 Mid 1st'] in page_probe2.json
reproduction.expected: Searching '2026' offers the current rookie class's picks, the most-traded asset type in dynasty.
reproduction.actual: queries['2026 Pick 1.0'] = [] and queries['2026'] = [] (no pick rows); queries['2027 Mid 1st'] = ['2027 Mid 1st PICK #48.0 · 5,606'].

userImpact: A user cannot build the most common dynasty trade shape — a current-class rookie pick for a player — through the page's primary control. The picks are still reachable via the global search popup, a KTC import or a share URL, so the omission reads as the app not having the asset rather than as a deliberate filter. Nothing on screen explains the exclusion.

priorFinding.note: Area-2 priors do not cover the asset picker.

whatWorks: resolvePickRow correctly maps every Sleeper label shape onto the slot-specific board rows ('2026 1st' -> '2026 Pick 1.06' @ 4,987, '2026 Mid 1st' -> '2026 Pick 1.06'), correctly skipping the suppressed generic-tier rows via row.raw.pickGenericSuppressed. The resolver is not the problem; the picker filter is.
rootCause: A hardcoded year literal repeated at four call sites, added to keep league-owned current-year picks out of generic suggestion pools, applied to the search box as well.
requiredRepair: Replace all four `/^2026\b/` literals with a predicate built from the memoised `currentDraftYear`, and drop the exclusion from searchAssets entirely (explicit user search is not a suggestion pool). If current-year picks must stay out of balancers, keep it there only and say so in the UI.

title: Pick original-owner identity is discarded before it reaches the trade calculator: 53 of 216 league picks collapse onto a duplicate name, and the duplicate guard then makes them untradeable
claimUnderTest: The trade calculator can represent a league team's real pick holdings. CLAUDE.md's draft-capital section treats pick ownership as real Sleeper-derived data.
observed: The contract's sleeper.teams[].pickDetails carries {season, round, slot, original_roster_id, owner_roster_id, label} for every pick — original_roster_id IS present and correct. The trade page reads only team.picks (the flat label array), where all of Jason's eight 2027 firsts are the identical string '2027 1st'. resolvePickRow maps every one of them to the tier-centre row '2027 Mid 1st' @ 5,606. teamRosterNames() then returns a Set, and addToSide() refuses any name already in the trade (`allTradeNames.has(row.name)`). Net effect measured on the live league: Jason holds 62 picks that resolve to 18 distinct row names; the league holds 216 picks that resolve to 163 distinct names — 53 picks are unrepresentable. A trade of two 2027 firsts cannot be built at all, and a rebuilding team's first is priced identically to a contender's.

reproduction.command: cd docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W08 && node picks.mjs && node picks3.mjs
reproduction.expected: 216 roster picks -> 216 addressable trade assets, each carrying its original owner.
reproduction.actual: 216 -> 163 distinct names (53 collapsed). Jason: 62 -> 18. His eight 2027 firsts (original_roster_id 1,2,3,6,8,9,10,12) all become '2027 Mid 1st' @ 5,606.

numericProof.formula: distinct(resolvePickRow(label).name for label in team.picks) summed over 12 teams

userImpact: A manager holding multiple firsts in the same year (the single most common consolidation-trade setup in dynasty) cannot model the trade. When one does fit, every future first is priced at the Mid tier regardless of whose it is — a 2027 first from the league's worst team and from its best are both 5,606, which is the difference between a fair trade and a fleecing.

priorFinding.note: Area-0 (draft/auction) priors cover the draft board; no area-2 prior covers pick identity inside the trade calculator.

whatWorks: pickDetails is fully populated with original_roster_id and owner_roster_id for all 216 picks — the data needed for the fix is already in the payload and is not being read. Pick label resolution itself is exhaustive (0 unresolved labels across all 12 teams).
rootCause: Assets are keyed by display NAME throughout the trade builder (addToSide, removeAssetFromSide, isAssetInTrade, filterPickerRows, serializeWorkspace, valueOverrides, destinations). Picks have no unique name, so identity collapses. team.picks was built as a label array before pickDetails existed and nothing migrated to it.
requiredRepair: Give trade assets a stable id (playerId for players, `${season}-${round}-${original_roster_id}` for picks) and key the trade sides on it instead of `name`. Short of that, at minimum render picks as '2027 1st (from Ed)' from pickDetails.original_roster_id so the names are distinct and the dedup guard stops eating them.
dependencies: Pricing a from-team pick differently requires a projected-standings input the platform does not have; the identity fix is independent of and prior to that.

title: 48 of 216 league roster picks and 260 of 1,072 board rows are addable to a trade at a silent value of 0
claimUnderTest: dynasty-data.js's SCALE CONTRACT comment: 'an unpriced row reports 0 and drops out of those sums rather than distorting them.' The trade calculator sums effectiveValue = row.values[valueMode].
observed: The drop-to-zero is real, but on /trade the row is still selectable and still occupies a side. 260 of 1,072 materialised rows (24%) carry rankDerivedValue null -> values.full 0. All 48 of the league's 2027/2028 5th- and 6th-round picks resolve to board rows with no value (2027 Mid 5th, 2027 Mid 6th, 2028 Mid 5th, 2028 Mid 6th — 12 of each). The search result row does mark it ('AJ Dillon RB — · 0'), which is honest, but once added the asset renders as a normal chip and contributes 0 to the side total, the gap, the verdict and the CSV export with no warning. Separately, all 18 2029 pick rows carry no _rawComposite, so in the 'Raw' value mode they contribute 0 while showing a non-zero value in 'Our Value'.

reproduction.command: cd docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W08 && node picks3.mjs && node rows.mjs
reproduction.expected: An asset the board declines to price is either excluded from the trade builder or flagged inside the trade with a 'not priced' badge.
reproduction.actual: zero-full rows: 260 of 1072; zero-raw rows: 18 (all 2029 picks); league roster picks resolving to value 0: 48 of 216, all 2027/2028 rounds 5-6.

userImpact: A trade of 'my 2028 6th for your 2028 6th' shows both sides at 0 and the verdict FAIR, which is coincidentally right. 'My 2028 5th for your Boye Mafe' shows the 5th at 0 and reads LOPSIDED, which overstates the imbalance and pushes the user to add more. Because the chip looks identical to a priced one, the user has no signal that the number is missing rather than small.
whatWorks: The search dropdown does render '— · 0' for an unpriced row, and inferValueBundle correctly refuses to fall back to the composite scale (the documented H1 fix holds — 0, not a composite-scale number).
rootCause: effectiveValue coerces a missing board value to 0 and no caller distinguishes 'worth zero' from 'not priced'. src/trade/finder.py already solves this pattern with metadata.assetsUnpricedByBoard; the client-side calculator has no equivalent.
requiredRepair: Carry an `isUnpriced` flag on the row (the contract already stamps rowsUnpricedByBoard), render the chip with a 'not priced' badge, and show a side-level note 'N assets on this side are not priced by the board' so the verdict is read with that caveat.

title: The 'Raw' value mode is not comparable across asset classes: one dropdown click turns a FAIR trade into UNFAIR and flips which side wins
claimUnderTest: dynasty-data.js documents `raw` as 'the legacy scraper composite, ~1.131x the canonical board (measured)' — i.e. a single global scale factor, which would leave every comparison unchanged. VALUE_MODES offers it as a peer of 'Our Value' with no caveat.
observed: The rawComposite/board ratio is not a constant: median 1.1034 for offense, 1.0467 for IDP, 1.0629 for picks — offense sits 5.4% heavier than IDP in Raw mode — and the per-player dispersion is far larger (p25 1.02, p75 1.21). Verified end to end in a real browser: Sam LaPorta (TE) and Sonny Styles (LB) both carry rankDerivedValue 5,222 on the live board. With the value-mode Select on 'Our Value' the meter reads '5,021 VS 5,222 | Gap: 201 | FAIR | Side B wins by 4%'. Selecting 'Raw' — no other change — the same trade reads '5,564 VS 4,180 | Gap: 1,384 | UNFAIR | Side A wins by 25%'. The verdict flips severity AND direction. Nothing in the UI says the two modes are on incomparable scales.

reproduction.expected: If raw is the board times a constant, a board-even trade stays even in Raw mode: gap 0 both ways.
reproduction.actual: Our Value gap 201 (FAIR, B wins 4%); Raw gap 1,384 (UNFAIR, A wins 25%). Class medians 1.1034 (offense) vs 1.0467 (IDP).

numericProof.formula: gap_raw = rawComposite(A) - rawComposite(B) for a pair with rankDerivedValue(A) == rankDerivedValue(B)

userImpact: A user who flips to 'Raw' to sanity-check a mixed offense/IDP trade gets a verdict that disagrees with the default one by 25 percentage points and names the other winner. In an IDP league — which this one is (356 IDP rows, 331 with a market value) — every cross-class trade is affected. There is no label telling the user which of the two answers to believe.

priorFinding.note: Adjacent to PRIOR-A02-F05 (Monte Carlo ignores the value mode) but that is a threading bug, not a scale-comparability defect.

whatWorks: The mode switch itself threads correctly through effectiveValue -> sideTotal -> adjustedSideTotals -> TradeMeter; the numbers rendered are exactly `_rawComposite`. The defect is that those numbers do not form a single scale.
rootCause: _rawComposite is per-source scraper output normalised within each source's own board (KTC for offense, IDPTradeCalc for IDP), never cross-normalised. The canonical pipeline's percentile/Hill step is what makes classes comparable, and Raw mode is defined as the value BEFORE that step.
requiredRepair: Either remove the Raw mode from the trade calculator (keep it on /rankings as a per-row diagnostic where no cross-row sum is taken), or gate it: when a trade spans more than one asset class in Raw mode, show 'Raw values are per-source and are not comparable across offense/IDP/picks' and suppress the verdict badge.

title: 'Copy KTC URL' hardcodes tep=0, sending a TE-premium league's trade to KTC's non-TE-premium board
claimUnderTest: 'Copy KTC URL' is offered as a second opinion on the same trade. CLAUDE.md states the whole board is anchored on ktcSfTep — 'the anchor IS the TE++ board' — and this league's scoring profile is superflex_tep15_ppr1 with bonusRecTe 0.5 (confirmed in the live contract's rankingsOverride).
observed: build_ktc_url hardcodes params = {var: 5, pickVal: 0, format: 2, isStartup: 0, tep: 0}. Every exported link asks keeptradecut.com to grade the trade on its NO-TE-premium board, while our own page graded it on the TE++ board. For any trade containing a TE the two answers must differ, and nothing in the copied URL or the 'KTC URL copied' toast says so. Secondary: the board's canonical current-year pick row names ('2026 Pick 1.06') are unresolvable by the exporter — it only knows KTC's tier labels ('2026 Mid 1st' -> id 1528) — so a trade containing a current-class pick exports without it.

reproduction.expected: tep set to match the league (bonusRecTe 0.5 -> KTC tep=1 or 2), and the slot pick resolved to KTC's nearest tier id.

numericProof.formula: exported tep param vs league TE premium

userImpact: The user opens the KTC link to check the app's verdict against the market and gets a KTC grade computed on the wrong format. Any disagreement on a TE trade is attributed to the app's model when it is actually a format mismatch, and the user may reverse a correct decision.
whatWorks: The pick DROP is honest: unresolved names are returned per side and the /trade toast renders them ('KTC URL copied — unmatched: 2026 Pick 1.06', page.jsx:1231-1238). import-ktc round-trips correctly, including picks (teamTwo=1528 -> '2026 Mid 1st', isPick true).
rootCause: A static params dict written before the board's TE++ anchoring was established; format=2 was parameterised in spirit but every value is a literal.
requiredRepair: Derive tep from the league registry's scoring profile (the contract already carries bonusRecTe and tepMultiplierDerived) and map the board's slot-pick names onto KTC's tier labels via pickAliases before resolving.

title: Trade verdict A->B / B->A symmetry is exact — verified on 20 real trades and 40,000 random ones
claimUnderTest: ktcAdjustPackage's branch structure is asymmetric on its face (BRANCH 2 and BRANCH 3 are hand-mirrored, and the V===1/V===2 sub-branches are not literal mirrors), which is exactly the shape that produces order dependence.
observed: It is nonetheless exactly symmetric in practice. Twenty trades built from real live-board assets across four shapes (1v2 elite consolidation, mixed offense+pick vs offense+IDP, IDP 1v2, 3v4 multi-asset) all produce gap(A,B) == -gap(B,A) to floating-point exactness (0 asymmetric of 20). A further 40,000 random 1-3 vs 1-3 trades produced no asymmetry. The backend Monte Carlo endpoint independently enforces this and reports it: POST /api/trade/simulate-mc returns symmetryCheck {winProbA_AB: 0.5012, winProbA_BA_flipped: 0.5016, drift: 0.0004, enforced: true} with method 'consensus_based_win_rate_symmetrized'.

reproduction.command: cd docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W08 && node rows.mjs && node symmetry.mjs && curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-w08.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/trade/simulate-mc -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"sideA":[{"name":"Sam LaPorta","rankDerivedValue":5222,"pos":"TE","team":"DET"}],"sideB":[{"name":"Sonny Styles","rankDerivedValue":5222,"pos":"LB","team":"PHI"}],"seed":42,"nSims":20000}'
reproduction.actual: trades: 20, asymmetric: 0. Monte Carlo drift 0.0004 with enforced:true.

priorFinding.note: F01 claims 'two share-link producers feed the same trade builder with opposite side semantics, so a trade opened from history simulates backwards'. That is a share-link/side-assignment claim, not a math-symmetry one; I did not probe the /trades history producer and cannot confirm or refute it. What I CAN state is that the verdict math itself is exactly order-independent, so any observed reversal must come from side assignment, not from the gap computation.

title: KTC Value Adjustment Python<->JS parity is exact: 0 differences over the 139-trade fixture, identical RMS 26.59 against KTC's captured displays
claimUnderTest: src/trade/ktc_va.py claims to be a 'verbatim translation' of the JS port and says parity 'is verified by tests/trade/test_ktc_va_python_port.py'. That test in fact only compares the PYTHON side against the fixture with a loose RMS<50 bound — it never runs the JS. So the stated verification did not exist as described.
observed: I ran both implementations over all 139 fixture trades directly and diffed them pairwise. Result: 0 mismatches on (value, side) — not merely 'both within tolerance of KTC', but bit-for-bit agreement — and identical RMS against KTC's observed displays: JS 26.59, Python 26.59. The repo's own test suite also passes: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/trade/test_ktc_va_python_port.py -q` -> 6 passed in 0.04s (Python 3.11.15; CI uses 3.12).

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/trade/test_ktc_va_python_port.py -q && cd docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W08 && node js_va.mjs && cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && .venv/bin/python -c "import json,math,sys; sys.path.insert(0,'.'); from src.trade.ktc_va import ktc_adjust_package; S='docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W08/'; fx=json.load(open('scripts/ktc_va_observations.json')); js=json.load(open(S+'js_va.json')); m=[i for i,o in enumerate(fx['observations']) if (lambda r:(r.value if r.displayed else 0, r.side if r.displayed else 0))(ktc_adjust_package(o.get('team1Values') or [], o.get('team2Values') or [])) != (js[i]['value'], js[i]['side'])]; print('mismatches', len(m))"
reproduction.expected: 0 mismatches if the port is verbatim.

userImpact: None — this works. The backend engines (angle finder, trade suggestions, Monte Carlo) grade a package identically to the /trade page.

priorFinding.note: F09 says three ports exist and none is tied to the others by a test, but 'None today — I executed all 139 fixture trades through all three: JS vs ktc_va.py = 0 differences'. Independently reproduced for the JS<->ktc_va.py pair. I did NOT re-run src/trade/market_value_adjustment.py, so F09's third leg stands unverified by me. The gap F09 identifies is real and my run does not close it: the repo still has no test that would catch a one-sided edit.

requiredRepair: Add a cross-implementation parity test (run the fixture through both and assert equality) so the property I measured by hand is actually pinned. See PRIOR-A02-F09.

title: The trade calculator shows no data freshness, no per-asset source count and no normalization confidence for the assets in the trade
claimUnderTest: The contract ships everything needed: dataFreshness {generatedAt, sourceTimestamps[key] = {mtime, ageHours, maxAgeHours, staleness}}, per-row marketConfidence, sourceCount, confidenceBucket/confidenceLabel, isSingleSource, hasSourceDisagreement, anomalyFlags.
observed: Full rendered DOM text of /trade contains no timestamp, no 'updated', no 'as of' and no staleness word anywhere. The asset chip renders name, position, an edge badge ('SELL 11%') and 'Consensus 69.2' — which is blendedSourceRank, a RANK, not a confidence. confidenceMeta() ('High/Moderate/Low consensus') exists in trade-sections.jsx but is wired ONLY into SuggestionCard (line 885), never into the calculator's own asset rows or verdict. So a trade built entirely from single-source, low-confidence rows renders identically to one built from 14-source consensus rows, and a board scraped days ago renders identically to a fresh one.

reproduction.command: cd docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W08 && /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket/.venv/bin/python page_probe3.py && python3 -c "import json;t=json.load(open('page_probe3.json'))['bodyText'];print([w for w in ['Updated','updated','as of','stale','fresh','ago','confidence','Confidence'] if w in t])"
reproduction.expected: At least a generatedAt/staleness line, since the contract carries it and /api/dynasty-data reports staleness per source.
reproduction.actual: [] — none of those tokens appear in the rendered /trade DOM. The contract meanwhile reports dataFreshness.generatedAt 2026-08-04T20:12:02Z and per-source ageHours/staleness for every source.

userImpact: A user executes a trade off a number with no way to know whether it rests on 14 sources or 1, or whether the scrape behind it is two hours or two days old. Combined with W08-F006 (unpriced rows render as 0), the calculator presents four qualitatively different states — well-sourced, thin, unpriced, stale — as one identical-looking number.
whatWorks: The 'Second opinions' > per-source breakdown panel does disclose coverage per vendor per side (coverage counts and imputedCounts, with an explicit impute-uncovered toggle) — that panel is honest. It is collapsed by default and is not the verdict.
rootCause: The freshness/confidence fields were added to the contract for /rankings and the terminal; /trade was never wired to them.
requiredRepair: Render dataFreshness.generatedAt + worst-source staleness in the trade-controls Panel, and put confidenceMeta(row.confidenceBucket) + sourceCount on the asset chip (both already computed).

title: The /trade page renders two different boards at once: the client calculator sums the TEP-overridden values while POST /api/trade/simulate on the same page answers from the un-overridden canonical board
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'every engine reads exactly one value — rankDerivedValue', presented as the guarantee that engine output and page output agree.
observed: They read the same FIELD but from different BOARDS. The client calculator's values come from POST /api/rankings/overrides?view=delta with the frontend's default tep_multiplier (W08-F001), while post_trade_simulate reads the process-global latest_contract_data, which no override touches. Measured on the same page in the same session: /trade renders Sam LaPorta at 5,021; POST /api/trade/simulate with playersIn:['Sam LaPorta'] returns delta.byPosition.TE.value = 5222 and receiving[0].value = 5222. Two numbers for one player, 201 points apart, both on screen. The gap reaches 21% for the worst-affected TEs.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-w08.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/trade/simulate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"teamName":"Jason","playersIn":["Sam LaPorta"],"playersOut":["Sonny Styles"]}' | python3 -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print('simulate says', d['receiving'][0]['value'])" && cd docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W08 && /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket/.venv/bin/python page_probe5.py
reproduction.expected: Both surfaces report the same value for the same player.
reproduction.actual: simulate says 5222; the /trade meter renders 5,021 for the same asset in the same session.

userImpact: The roster-impact panel and the fairness meter on the same screen disagree about what an asset is worth. A user checking 'does this improve my team' against 'is this fair' gets answers derived from two boards, and neither says which.

priorFinding.note: F03 ('One card shows three different fairness answers for the same trade') is about the fairness card's internal disagreement. This is a different axis: the same PLAYER carries two different values on one page because the client and the server resolve different boards. Same family of defect, different mechanism.

whatWorks: post_trade_simulate is otherwise correct: it never mutates latest_contract_data, correctly resolves the team via the session's Sleeper user_id, stamps leagueKey and valuationMode, and returns a coherent before/after/delta.
rootCause: The rankings-override pipeline is a client-side merge; nothing propagates the user's override map to server-side engines. Every engine endpoint accepts valuation_mode but none accepts source/TEP overrides.
requiredRepair: Fix W08-F001 first — once the frontend stops posting a redundant override, both surfaces resolve the same board and this closes with no further change. If per-user overrides ever become genuinely customised, the engines need the override map threaded the way valuation_mode already is.

title: Duplicate-asset protection works: an asset cannot appear twice on one side, cannot appear on both sides, and the KTC-import bulk path applies the same guard
claimUnderTest: An asset that appears on both sides, or twice on one side, would double-count into the side totals and the VA piece counts.
observed: addToSide() checks `allTradeNames` — a Set flattened across ALL sides, not just the target one — and returns early, then checks the target side again. searchAssets() also excludes anything in allTradeNames so the duplicate is never offered. The KTC-import bulk path deliberately bypasses addToSide and re-implements the guard with a shared `seen` Set spanning both sides (page.jsx:1134-1148), with a comment saying exactly that. filterPickerRows() in trade-logic.js has the same guard but is exported and never called by the app — dead code (see PRIOR-A02-F12).

reproduction.command: cd docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W08 && /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket/.venv/bin/python page_probe2.py   # queries['Josh Allen'] returns the row; after adding it, re-searching 'Josh Allen' returns no addable result
reproduction.expected: No path allows the same asset name into two side slots.
reproduction.actual: Confirmed by code trace on all four add paths (search, balancer, popup registerAddToTrade, KTC import) plus the browser probe. Caveat: the guard is keyed on `name`, which is exactly why picks with a shared name become unrepresentable — see W08-F005.

numericProof.formula: count(add paths lacking a cross-side dedup guard)

userImpact: None — this works. The name-keyed implementation has a real cost, but it is the pick-identity defect (W08-F005), not a double-count.

title: CLAUDE.md's KTC<->IDPTradeCalc comparability claim holds on the median but its stated dispersion band is stale — p90 measured 1.125 against a documented 1.054
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'of KTC's 500 rows, 475 also appear on the IDPTC board at a median value ratio of 1.000 (p10 0.888, p90 1.054, measured 2026-07-26). Both top out at 9999, so there is no rescaling to apply between them.'
observed: Re-measured on the live 2026-08-04 contract. 474 rows carry both ktcSfTep and idpTradeCalc (the claim's 475 within one row — confirmed). Median ratio 1.0030 (claim: 1.000 — confirmed). Both boards top out at 9999 (confirmed). But the dispersion has widened and shifted: p10 0.9216 (claimed 0.888) and p90 1.1252 (claimed 1.054). The p90 error is 6.7 points of value ratio — at the top of the board that is ~670 points on a 9999 scale. Note also that 0 of 356 IDP rows carry a ktcSfTep value at all, so 'directly comparable' rests entirely on the 474-row offense overlap; the comparability of the IDP-only tail is inferred, not measured. On the trade calculator specifically, no raw KTC value is ever summed with a raw IDPTradeCalc value: effectiveValue reads values.full (the blended board) for both, and the per-source breakdown sums each vendor only against itself with explicit coverage counts.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-w08.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data?view=app' -o /tmp/c.json && python3 -c "import json,statistics as st; d=json.load(open('/tmp/c.json')); r=sorted(p['ktcSfTep']/p['idpTradeCalc'] for p in d['players'].values() if p.get('ktcSfTep') and p.get('idpTradeCalc')); q=lambda x:r[int(x*(len(r)-1))]; print('n=%d median=%.4f p10=%.4f p90=%.4f'%(len(r),st.median(r),q(.1),q(.9)))"
reproduction.expected: n=475 median=1.000 p10=0.888 p90=1.054 per CLAUDE.md.

numericProof.formula: p90 of ktcSfTep/idpTradeCalc over rows carrying both

userImpact: Indirect. The claim is cited in CLAUDE.md as the justification for treating the two markets as peers in the pick-anchor set and the finder's per-market gate. The median holds so the conclusion survives, but a reader budgeting error from the documented band will under-estimate it by ~2x on the upper tail.

priorFinding.note: Prompt asked this claim be tested on the live payload rather than accepted; recorded as a measured confirmation-with-correction, not a defect.

whatWorks: The core claim (median 1.000, shared 9999 ceiling, no rescaling needed) reproduces. The trade calculator does NOT mix raw board values across markets — both classes go through the blended board.
rootCause: A measurement stamped 2026-07-26 quoted as a standing property; source boards drift.
requiredRepair: Re-state the band with its measurement date and re-measure on a cadence, or drop the p10/p90 from the doc and keep only the median + ceiling facts, which are the load-bearing ones.

title: POST /api/trade/simulate-mc answers an empty trade with a confident 'Coin-flip trade (~50%)' verdict and nSims 0 instead of an error
claimUnderTest: The route validates its body (400 invalid_body, 400 sides_must_be_lists) and clamps nSims to [1000, SIMULATE_MC_MAX_SIMS], implying no run can report fewer than 1000 sims.
observed: build_trade_player() drops every unparseable entry, so a body with the wrong side keys — or genuinely empty sides — yields side_a = side_b = [] and the route still returns 200 with winProbA 0.5, winProbB 0.5, nSims 0, riskLevel 'high', tierImpact 'even' and decisionSummary 'Coin-flip trade (~50%, delta=+0 even, risk high)'. nSims 0 contradicts the documented clamp floor of 1000, and 'coin-flip' is a verdict about a trade that does not exist.

reproduction.expected: 400 with an explicit 'no valid assets on either side', or at minimum nSims >= 1000 per the documented clamp.

numericProof.formula: nSims reported for an empty body

userImpact: Low today — MonteCarloButton is gated on the trade having assets, so the UI does not hit this. It matters as a contract defect: any future caller that mis-shapes the body (the shape is sideA/sideB, not the sides[] the rest of the page uses) gets a plausible-looking verdict instead of an error, and the mis-shape is silent.
whatWorks: With a correct body the endpoint is sound: symmetry enforced and reported (drift 0.0004), the contract's labelHint + disclaimer are returned, and the /trade UI does render a 'NOT a real-world win probability' warning (MonteCarloButton.jsx:237) — though it hardcodes the text rather than rendering the backend's disclaimer field, so the two can drift.
rootCause: Silent-drop parsing (build_trade_player returning None) with no post-parse emptiness check.
requiredRepair: After building side_a/side_b, return 400 when both are empty, and report how many entries were dropped so a mis-shaped body is diagnosable.
